report:
# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Act Obligations Apply?

## Executive Summary
The application date for high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III of the EU AI Act has shifted from the originally legislated date of 2 August 2026 to **2 December 2027**, following a Digital Omnibus/AI Omnibus amendment negotiated between the Council and Parliament (medium confidence) ([Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [SIG Summary](https://www.softwareimprovementgroup.com/blog/eu-ai-act-summary)). This deferral is reported to have entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/en/apply-ai-alliance/community-content/eu-ai-act-and-recruitment-why-december-2027-extension-prep-window-not-free-pass), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)), though the specific fixed calendar date of 2 December 2027 itself carries only medium confidence given some reliance on legal-analysis sources rather than official EU text. Separately, high-risk obligations tied to Annex I (product-embedded AI systems) now apply from 2 August 2028 rather than the originally planned 2 August 2027. Some sources have not yet caught up with this amendment and continue to cite the outdated 2 August 2026 date, creating confusion in publicly available guidance.

## Key Findings

### Original Legal Framework
As originally adopted, Article 113 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 set the general date of application of the AI Act at 2 August 2026, with Chapter III Sections 1–3 — covering the Annex III high-risk obligations — falling under this general application date ([IMMC.COM(2025)836](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025PC0836), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-113)) (high confidence). Article 111(2) also provided transitional rules so that operators of high-risk systems placed on the market before the application date would only be subject to the Regulation if those systems underwent significant design changes thereafter (medium confidence) ([Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

### The Delay: Digital Omnibus / AI Omnibus Amendment
On 19 November 2025, the European Commission proposed delaying Chapter III Sections 1–3 obligations (including Annex III) by up to 16 months, tying the start date to Commission confirmation that needed standards and tools were available (high confidence) ([IMMC.COM(2025)836](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025PC0836), [Akin Gump](https://www.akingump.com/en/insights/alerts/EU-AI-act-amendments-defer-and-clarify-obligations)). The Council and Parliament reached political agreement on 7 May 2026 to simplify and streamline the rules along these lines, adjusting the high-risk timeline and extending SME-type exemptions to small mid-caps (medium confidence) ([Consilium press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

Following these negotiations, the amended legislation is reported to have fixed concrete calendar dates rather than a conditional mechanism: **2 December 2027** for Annex III (Article 6(2)) high-risk systems, and **2 August 2028** for Annex I (Article 6(1)) high-risk systems (medium confidence) ([Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [SIG Summary](https://www.softwareimprovementgroup.com/blog/eu-ai-act-summary)). Multiple sources separately report that this deferral has entered into force, with the amendment in effect since 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/en/apply-ai-alliance/community-content/eu-ai-act-and-recruitment-why-december-2027-extension-prep-window-not-free-pass), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)). A transitional rule analogous to the original Article 111(2) is understood to apply operators-only obligations from the new dates onward for systems undergoing significant design changes (medium confidence) ([Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)).

### Related Enforcement Dates
Separately, transparency obligations and new prohibitions retain earlier dates: 2 August 2026 for transparency obligations and 2 December 2026 for certain prohibitions, according to the AI Act Service Desk FAQ (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-enforcement-start)). The Commission is also conducting a targeted consultation on draft guidelines for classifying high-risk AI systems, with the deadline extended past the original 23 June date (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy consultation](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/consultations/targeted-consultation-draft-guidelines-classification-high-risk-artificial-intelligence-systems)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several lower-confidence sources — apparently drafted before the Omnibus amendment took effect — still state that Annex III obligations became enforceable on 2 August 2026 (low confidence; flagged below 0.4) ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [OrbiqHQ](https://www.orbiqhq.com/eu-regulations/eu-ai-act-compliance), [Valuemate](https://www.valuemate.it/en/eu-ai-act-whitepaper.html)). One source explicitly issued a correction acknowledging an earlier claim of 2 August 2026 enforcement was wrong, confirming the shift to 2 December 2027 ([McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)). There is also inconsistency regarding Annex I timing — originally 2 August 2027, now cited as 2 August 2028 — reflecting the same legislative update. Sources differ on whether the delay mechanism remained conditional (tied to Commission confirmation of standards) or was replaced by fixed calendar dates in the final text, and no official EU source in this dataset directly confirms the fixed-date outcome with high confidence.

## Knowledge Gaps
The precise official citation of the amending regulation (referred to variously as "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744," the "Digital Omnibus," or "AI Omnibus") is not consistently confirmed. It remains unclear whether the conditional 16-month delay mechanism survived in the final text or was fully replaced by fixed dates. The interaction between interim obligations (transparency, prohibitions) and Annex III-classified systems before December 2027 is unaddressed, as are potential sector- or deployer-specific carve-outs within the Annex III timeline.
